name: 1906 Prairie Avenue — the Edson Keith house (Italianate stone front; attached 1908)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick with stone front dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2329) in place by T-3238 (piece 1 of T-1898), under the draft's own id, as a K01 stone-front Italianate house read off the Chicagology wood engraving of the Edson Keith residence (chicagology_1906_keith_engraving) and the 1906 vignette of the Chicago Tribune's 9 January 1898 strip (chicago_tribune_1898_01_09_residence_district) against the 1911 sheet's plan (s28fp-1906-b1): two storeys over a raised basement under a low hipped roof and a deep bracketed cornice; a canted bay at the front's south end rising a stage past the cornice as a tower; the round-arched door under a porch on columns whose flat top is a balustraded balcony before the arched window over the door; a high stoop between scrolled cheeks onto a balustraded terrace; arched, hooded windows; the sheet's south-flank range and rear wing in brick. 1908, which the sheet draws attached and the T-1841 census rules one building with 1906, is this record's north end. The Chicagology mansard photograph labelled 1906 is the 1900 house (the census ruling r28-1900-1906-photo; T-3239 weighed it: its mansard, dormers and corner bay are not the hip-roofed, towered front both the engraving and the vignette draw). T-3239 solved the vignette's camera, set aside the Tribune's 1896 item (a lakeshore scene, no view of the house), weighed the c. 1914 elevation drawing (1906 third from the south on the west side), lowered and broadened the tower, widened the porch and set the balustrade on the terraces. T-3239 then built the two things it had left open: the hip cut off at a railed deck (k01_hip_deck) with its stacks raised over it, and on the south flank the sheet's stone range stood as the engraving's two-storey wing with a columned porch in the angle before it under a balustraded balcony (side_porch), retiring the 1.5 m brick strip. What the pictures do not show is reconstructed and listed under liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the Tribune drew its front in January 1898 with the composition of the undated engraving; nothing read so far records an alteration before 1904.

position.symbolic_location: 1906 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1906 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 22.500, v -2.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation -0.617 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: Two storeys over a raised basement in the engraving and in the 1898 vignette, the south bay rising a third stage as a tower; the 1911 sheet's '3B' is read as counting the raised basement, whose lights stand clear of grade under the terrace.

construction.note: '3B brick with stone front' on the 1911 sheet; the census ruling r28-1900-1906-photo calls 1906 a brownstone front.

principal_floor_m.note: The terrace and the porch floor at the stoop's head: the 1898 vignette draws the stoop at about thirteen risers between its cheeks, about 2.4 m at 0.18 m a riser; the engraving's terrace stands at the same height over its basement lights.

storey_heights_m.note: The principal storey 4.4 m and the chamber storey 5.4 m, through the engraving's solved camera: the chamber's round-headed windows stand about 3 m tall, from sills just over the porch's balcony rail to crowns about 0.95 m under the cornice's bed, and the principal windows' crowns about 0.8 m under the chamber sills; the taller upper storey is the proportion 1612 Prairie's photograph gave (4.15 and 5.38 m). An engraving may stretch its heights, so the camera's solve states the fit, and T-3239 weighs them against the vignette.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the rules' stone front. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the rules' brick flank. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the one K03 panel K01 lays on the brick flanks and rear, which neither picture shows in colour. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

stone_front.note: The sheet's stone front, laid as brownstone on the census ruling r28-1900-1906-photo ('1906 was a brownstone front'); its dressing and the base's rusticated course is the engraving's ashlar lines over its basement lights, and the colour is the ruling's, not a picture's.

wall_head.note: The register's and the engraving's deep bracketed cornice: paired scrolled brackets over a panelled frieze on the front and the south flank, the frieze's panels drawn between them. Its paint is reconstructed, a brown with the stone.

roof_form.note: A low hipped roof over the cornice in the engraving, its slopes running back from the front's eave; its top deck and the balustrade the engraving draws on it are open for T-3239.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The hip's slopes, low behind the cornice in the engraving.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's corona stands well out over its brackets, about 0.75 m on the engraving's proportions.

roof_covering.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a low hip's tin, which a monochrome engraving does not say. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

stair_tread_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the rules' tread. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The porch's floor at the stoop's head, about as deep as its columns stand out from the wall in the engraving.

stoop_width_m.note: The stoop between its cheeks, about as wide as the door's arch and its jambs in the vignette.

door_clear_height_m.note: The round-arched double door, about as tall as the principal storey's windows in the vignette.

entrance_bay.note: The door is the first opening column north of the south bay, under the porch, in both pictures.

front_bays.note: A blind column between the south bay and the porch (no opening of its own), the door's column and one window column north of it, the engraving's two columns on the front's lit face; the south bay stands south of the door (the vignette's composition) and the north end is the sheet's stone front's north end.

sash_by_storey.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the flanks' and rear's sash, which no picture measures. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

side_bays.note: The south flank's front window column, between the south bay and the porch. T-3239: two round-headed lights a storey on the flank between the wing and that column, behind the porch's columns and over its balcony, as the engraving draws them (two arched lights over the balcony, arched openings behind the columns); their places between the columns and their sizes the flank's sash (sash_by_storey) are inferred, their heads read.

north_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the north flank stands against 1908's attached wing, so it has no windows. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the rear wall south of the rear wing is left unlit; its windows are the rear wing's. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

window_kit.note: Round-headed windows under hood moulds in both storeys of the front in the engraving and the vignette; their sash is K06's round-headed fanlight sash.

street_front_openings.note: The front's openings in the engraving: the door's column carries the arched window over the porch's balcony; the north column a tall round-headed window in each storey, each under a hood with a keystone, and a round-headed basement light under the terrace.

street_front_dress.note: The engraving's belt at the terrace, the stone to the cornice and the frieze's panels between the brackets.

entrance_kit.note: The porch on columns at the stoop's head, its flat top a balcony with a stone balustrade before the arched window over the door (the vignette: 'a flat portico with balustraded balcony and arched window above'; the engraving: its columns and balcony); the terrace across the front from the south bay (v 5.5) to the end of the sheet's stone front (v 15.25), and on it and down the stoop's cheeks a turned stone balustrade, which both the engraving and the vignette draw (T-3239; its profile, pitch and newels are 1620 Prairie's, reconstructed); the stoop's scrolled cheeks are the engraving's curved flights' ends, where the vignette draws a straight flight ending at block newels. The porch is 5.0 m wide, the vignette's portico on its solved camera (about 4.7 m; T-3239, where T-3238 had 4.0 m); the vignette draws its top as a flat entablature, the engraving as the balustraded balcony built.

bays.note: The south bay: canted, standing on grade at the front's south end under its own bracketed cornice and a low cap with cresting, in both the vignette and the engraving; three round-headed lights a stage. T-3239 re-read it on the vignette's solved camera (tribune_1898_front): about 5.5 m across against the door-to-window spacing, so a 2.6 m ring (v 0.4-5.6), and three tiers of lights over the basement with its cap just over the main cornice, as the c. 1914 elevation drawing also stops it; so four stages of 2.34, 4.4, 3.5 and 3.0 m, its wall head 13.24 m, 1.1 m over the main wall's 12.14 m (K01's least is 1.0 m). The stage heights within that are reconstructed. The south wing (T-3239): the 1911 sheet's stone range on the flank's rear part (s28fp-1906-b1 p5, about u -1.5 to 8.5 and 2.3 m out from the main wall), stood as the engraving's two-storey block: s 0-8.6 and 2.3 m out in the front's stone, round-headed lights two a storey in its south face and one in its east face over the porch's balcony, the house's bracketed cornice carried round it at the main bed and a stone balustrade round its flat top. It retires the sheet's 1.5 m brick strip T-3238 stood along the whole flank; the strip's front part is where the engraving draws the porch (side_porch). The wing's windows' places and the flat top (the engraving draws a short hip under a railed deck) are reconstructed. The basement lights under the parlour floor (a light under each of the tower's three faces, as each stage above has, and two under the wing) are reconstructed: neither picture reads that low, and the front's own basement lights are the precedent.

rear_wings.note: The sheet's rear wing behind the main body's north half (s28fp-1906-b1, rectangle r3), at the main body's floors; its windows and roof are reconstructed.

chimneys.note: RECONSTRUCTED: three stacks on the flank walls; the engraving draws a tall stack over the south flank, which T-3239 places. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238. T-3239: the hip now stops at its deck (hip_deck), and the engraving's tall stack rises well over the deck's rail, so the stacks' tops stand 2.4 m over the deck.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the rules' gutters and pipes, behind the front. Liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

boundary.note: The engraving's low stone wall along the walk, panelled between square piers, with the stoop's opening; its line is the 1904 parcel's street line (draft_plan street_u 31.417) and its ends the lot's.

yard.note: T-3206's rule (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures), for the house T-3238 put onto K01. The stoop comes down square to the front wall's opening (s 8.0-10.4); the walk runs from the stoop's foot out through it to the public walk, 1.5 m wide, with the app's own ground either side. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's flags, their width and wear are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238.

side_porch.note: The engraving's porch on the south flank, in the angle the south wing makes with the main wall: round columns with square capitals over the terrace's podium, under an entablature whose top is a balcony railed by a balustrade before the wing's arched east light and the flank's upper lights (k01_porte_cochere's side_porch, T-3239). Its place is the angle between the wing (s 0-8.6, the 1911 sheet's stone range) and the flank's front window column; the engraving's flank does not hold the front's perspective (the camera's solve), so its length is not read through the camera: 6 m, three columns as the engraving draws three, its depth the wing's 2.3 m as the balcony's front runs on from the wing's south face. The floor is the terrace's (the principal floor, 2.34 m) and the deck the chamber floor (6.74 m), as the balcony stands under the chamber lights. The 1911 sheet draws a 1.5 m brick strip along this stretch of the flank, which may be the porch enclosed by then; the engraving is followed (liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238). The columns' and capitals' sizes, the entablature's and the balustrade's sections are reconstructed, the balustrade the front porch's.

hip_deck.note: The engraving's railed deck over the main hip, its slopes short from the cornice to a level top railed all round with posts at its corners; the c. 1914 elevation drawing also draws the hip flat-topped. Built by k01_hip_deck (T-3241's kit): the 25 degree hip cut off level at 13.3 m, about 1.5 m over its eave, and a rail 0.8 m high round the deck's edge. The deck's height is read loosely off the engraving's proportions (the roof is foreshortened); the rail is the kit's pierced parapet where the engraving draws a balustrade, a difference under a foot at the street (liberty L-k01-1906-keith-3238).
